claims.text: Simultaneous wear-corrosion resistance is governed by the dynamic formation and maintenance of a dense passive film supported by a refined nanocrystalline subsurface.
The passive film is self-healing during sliding contact.
A refined subsurface microstructure promotes a chemically uniform, adherent, corrosion-inhibiting oxide or compound layer.
The refined microstructure accommodates strain during sliding and thereby limits crack initiation and abrasive wear.
The CoCrFeNiMo-based baseline has a relatively coarse microstructure and less-developed passive-film formation.
Process modification or microalloying can be used to produce a significantly refined or nanocrystalline subsurface in the modified coating.
Refinement of the subsurface enhances the rapid formation and stability of the passive protective film.
Nanocrystalline refinement increases the density and homogeneity of grain boundaries, which act as rapid pathways for passive-film formation.
Mo and Cr promote formation of the protective passive film under mechanical stress.
The passive layer reduces the area available for corrosive attack.
The passive layer acts as a solid lubricant and mitigates wear.
Passive-film protection establishes a synergistic coupling between wear resistance and corrosion protection.
Compared with the coarse baseline, the refined variant will have lower friction coefficient, lower wear rate, and lower corrosion current density during simultaneous tribocorrosion.
When the passive film remains intact because of nanocrystalline support, total combined degradation and both of its wear and corrosion components will be reduced.
The refinement benefit diminishes when mechanical removal exceeds the passive film's formation or recovery rate.
The protective effect should hold under moderate wear loads at room temperature in 3.5 wt.% NaCl when the film can reform dynamically.
The protective effect may fail under extremely high mechanical stresses, very high temperatures, or highly aggressive media that irreversibly damage the film.
Prior studies report enhanced tribocorrosion or combined wear-corrosion performance in tailored HEA coatings.
A CoCrFeNiMo0.85 HEA coating provides corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at room temperature.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and corrosion current density, or failure to observe enhanced passive-film integrity, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The comparison is described as using identical processing routes, but the refined variant may be created by changing process parameters or by microalloying. Either option changes an additional variable beyond microstructure, so the proposed pair is not necessarily composition- and processing-matched.
